what: `SOME_CONST = 14;` (a path to a const as a destructuring assignment left-hand side) gets no error: hir-def lowers it as a path pattern and hir-ty accepts it as a const pattern. rustc (extract_unit_struct_path / extract_tuple_struct_path in rustc_ast_lowering/src/expr.rs) keeps a path or call that resolves to something that is no constructor as an expression, so it is E0070 invalid left-hand side. Report it as hir::NotAStructPath with StructPathFound::Def(Const) on the PathExpr (blaze-diagnostics now lowers a Def found on a CallExpr/PathExpr to E0070), or as InvalidLhsOfAssignment. Test: tests::bodies::calls::an_assignment_to_a_constant_a_literal_and_a_call (tests/ui/error-codes/E0070.rs, line 6).

history.note: hir-def expr_store/lower.rs path_is_destructuring_assignment now takes the constructor shape the form needs, as rustc expected_in_unit_struct_pat / expected_in_tuple_struct_pat: a bare path is a pattern only for a unit struct or unit variant, a call only for a tuple struct or tuple variant; Self is SelfCtor (pattern). A const, function, static or constructor of the other form stays an expression, so hir-ty check_lhs_assignable reports E0070 (InvalidLhsOfAssignment). Before, a const path and every call were patterns. Test expr_store::tests::body::an_assignment_destructures_only_through_a_constructor_of_its_form.
